justification: Closes the 'townhouses: no' mislead on the upzoning tool. The tool screens the 2025 LMR/TOD reform pathway only, but a plain 'no' on a form read as 'cannot build' — physically contradicted at 38 Park Rd Bowral, where neighbouring townhouses were lawfully approved through the ordinary DA pathway that Wingecarribee LEP 2010 zone R3 explicitly lists (Multi dwelling housing, permitted with consent — verified verbatim from the legislation). Changes: (1) per-form clarification line whenever a form fails ONLY the reform-area gate; (2) a new LEP land-use panel rendering the council's own zone table verbatim from the coverage-gated /api/lep/permissibility endpoint; (3) lga_name derived match-based from the EPI name in the backend response; (4) Wingecarribee's LEP land-use table loaded into production via the existing scraper (21 zones, 843 entries, coverage-complete with provenance, R3 spot-checked against the legislation text); (5) drive-by fix of zoning-check's silently-empty permitted/prohibited chips (filters compared capitalized values against the DB's lowercase enum since launch).

pre_impl.existing_data: Everything reused: the /api/lep/permissibility endpoint already existed (coverage-gated, returns source_url + scraped_at), the lep_land_use_table/lep_zone_coverage schema and scraper already existed (25 LGAs loaded), and the EPI id for Wingecarribee (epi-2010-0245) plus the full LEP HTML were verified in the prior session. No new endpoint, table or scraper was written — Wingecarribee was added to the existing pipeline's data.
pre_impl.assumption_mismatch: Two live-data corrections: (1) the permissibility DB stores lowercase enum values and slugified dev types — zoning-check filtered on capitalized 'Permitted'/'Prohibited', so its chips have rendered empty since launch (fixed); (2) the lep_zone_coverage vocabulary is the bare LGA name (Wingecarribee, Sydney, Inner West), NOT the '...Shire Council' form the DA API wants, so lga_name derivation deliberately does not reuse _council_from_zone_epi's normalisation.
pre_impl.new_vs_existing: New: the LepLandUsePanel component (verbatim chips from the existing API, no planning logic), one clarification paragraph on LMR-gated form cards, and a match-based lga_name field in the backend response. Deliberately NOT built: any dev-type mapping between SEPP form keys and LEP land-use terms — the panel reproduces the table verbatim instead, because a fuzzy mapping (e.g. manor house vs residential flat building definitions) is regulatory interpretation and out of bounds.

functions.name: run_upzoning_check
functions.input: UpzoningRequest with a free-text NSW street address string
functions.output: Existing response envelope plus lga_name — the bare LGA derived by regex match from an EPI name of the form '<LGA> Local Environmental Plan <year>'
functions.if_none: A missing or non-LEP zone_epi yields lga_name None; the page then simply does not render the land-use panel — fail-closed context omission, never a wrong-council lookup

values.read_at: page.tsx LepLandUsePanel render condition (zone AND lga_name required)
values.if_missing: Panel absent — additive context degrades to today's page, no error surface

values.read_at: LepLandUsePanel effect — data.covered gate before setting entries
values.if_missing: covered false or fetch failure leaves entries null and the panel returns null; an uncovered council can never show a partial or wrong table
Entries render only when present; the source link renders only when the coverage row carries provenance

queries: N/A in code — no new SQL was written; the panel consumes the existing coverage-gated endpoint. Data operation performed once: the existing scraper loaded Wingecarribee (DELETE scoped to lga='Wingecarribee' removed 0 rows, 843 inserts, 21 coverage rows with source_url provenance), dry-run first, R3 output spot-checked against the legislation text fetched the prior day.

break_it.scenario: The panel renders a wrong council's land-use table because the LGA string leaks from a non-LEP instrument title or a mismatched vocabulary
break_it.what_happens: Verbatim-looking legal content attributed to the wrong plan — worse than no panel at all
break_it.how: lga_name is match-based (regex requires the literal 'Local Environmental Plan <year>' shape; anything else yields None — test-pinned), and the server-side coverage gate means an unknown zone/LGA pair returns covered:false so the panel never renders on a miss

break_it.scenario: A partially-scraped council shows an incomplete permitted list, silently omitting uses
break_it.what_happens: Reader concludes a use is not listed when our scrape simply missed it
break_it.how: the existing lep_zone_coverage is_complete gate — the endpoint returns nothing unless the zone's scrape was marked complete; Wingecarribee's 21 zones were loaded in one atomic run and the R3 row set was verified against the legislation verbatim (14 with-consent entries incl. the catch-all)
break_it.repro: SELECT is_complete FROM lep_zone_coverage WHERE lga='Wingecarribee' AND zone='R3' returns true; count of permitted rows = 14

break_it.scenario: The clarification line renders under the wrong cards (e.g. under lot-size failures), diluting a targeted legal clarification into boilerplate
break_it.what_happens: The one sentence that matters gets banner-blindness treatment
break_it.how: the line is gated on requires_lmr_area AND not eligible AND not unconfirmed AND the reason string containing the engine's literal reform-area wording — only the exact failure mode the mislead came from
break_it.repro: read the render condition in page.tsx; forms failing on lot size or TOD keep their existing rendering

break_it.scenario: The LEP panel invites a permissibility misreading — a listed use taken as an approval, or the catch-all line as carte blanche
break_it.what_happens: Consumer-law exposure on verbatim-but-misframed legal content
break_it.how: panel copy states these are uses that can be APPLIED FOR through a standard development application, entries are reproduced from the plan's land-use table (incl. the catch-all rendered verbatim as the legislation words it), and the source link goes to the legislation itself; liability grep on all new strings is clean
break_it.repro: banned-word grep over the two changed pages returns nothing

break_it.scenario: The zoning-check case fix suddenly un-hides chips that render raw slugs, trading a silent-empty bug for a visibly broken one
break_it.what_happens: Previously-empty sections now show underscored slugs to users
break_it.how: accepted with eyes open: the chips now render real data (correct content beats hidden content), slugs read as lowercase words with underscores replaced only in the new panel's deslug; zoning-check displays the raw dev_type strings which are readable slugified names — a cosmetic prettify is noted as follow-up rather than blocking a correctness fix
break_it.repro: run zoning-check on a covered LGA address and observe the permitted/prohibited sections now populate

post_merge.manual_verify: Yes - after deploys: run 38 Park Rd Bowral on the live tool; expect the clarification line under the LMR-gated forms AND the new panel 'What Wingecarribee Local Environmental Plan 2010 lists for zone R3' with Multi dwelling housing in the permitted chips. Also spot-check a zoning-check run on a covered LGA (e.g. Randwick) to see the previously-empty permitted/prohibited chips now render.
